stem: Facility rooting success is 85%, but one donor/batch combination is 52% while all others exceed 90%. What is the best analytical approach?
choices: Report the 85% facility rate as the primary conclusion because facility-level performance is the controlled KPI.
Exclude the 52% group as an outlier if all other donor/batch groups exceed 90%.
Retain the overall 85% metric but stratify and investigate the 52% donor/batch subgroup because the aggregate masks a localized performance problem.
Weight the highest-performing donor group more heavily so the facility metric reflects typical rather than exceptional performance.
rationale: An aggregate can be accurate while still hiding an important subgroup failure. The 85% facility rate should be retained, but the 52% donor/batch result deserves separate analysis because it differs sharply from the rest of the population. Automatically removing or reweighting the subgroup would erase the very signal that may identify a donor, handling, environment, or process problem.
